title: State (BSES YPL) v. Yasmeen
court: Addl. Sessions Judge-05 (Electricity), East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
result: Convicted u/s 135; posted for sentence (no settlement of theft bill reported)
statutes: Third proviso to Section 135(1) Electricity Act 2003

interpretations.interpretation: Puncturing the licensee's service cable at the pole and drawing supply through a wire so connected is a clause (a) tap — a connection at the pole-head or box is not required. 'Dishonestly' takes its s.24 IPC meaning (wrongful gain/wrongful loss).

Reverse-onus clause: proof of an artificial/unauthorised means raises a compulsory presumption of dishonest use (Neeraj Dutt) rebuttable on the prudent-man standard (Hiten P. Dalal); natural rebuttal is paid bills / lawful metered use, the s.106 Evidence Act onus lying on the consumer (Mukesh Rastogi).

citations.case: Punjab State Electricity Board v. Ashwani Kumar
citations.principle: An inspection report prepared by officers in discharge of official duty carries a presumption of regularity; onus on the consumer to rebut by cogent evidence.

citations.case: Sushil Sharma v. BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Non-examination of an independent/public witness is no infirmity where inspecting officials are trustworthy and bear no enmity to the accused.
'Shall presume' denotes a compulsory legal presumption the court is bound to draw until the fact is disproved.

citations.case: Hiten P. Dalal v. Bratindranath Banerjee
citations.principle: Rebuttal of a statutory presumption need not be conclusive; evidence must make the defence reasonably probable to a prudent man.

citations.case: Mukesh Rastogi v. North Delhi Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Easiest rebuttal of the theft presumption is production of paid electricity bills; Section 106 Evidence Act places that onus on the consumer.

significance.point: Puncturing a service cable is a clause (a) tap
significance.explanation: Piercing the licensee's service cable to bleed supply is itself the actionable connection.

significance.point: Identification in the videography anchors user status
significance.explanation: PW-3 identified the accused in the 65B-certified video; identity of accused and premises never disputed.

significance.point: Ownership documents seized in investigation reinforce occupancy
significance.explanation: IO seized the premises' ownership papers, pre-empting a premises-not-mine defence.

significance.point: No settlement was needed for conviction
significance.explanation: Conviction rests wholly on the unrebutted presumption and inspection evidence.

significance.point: A filed 65B certificate forecloses the videography challenge
significance.explanation: With Ex.PW2/B on record, the video's admissibility was not seriously contestable.

generic_facts.theft_mode: direct theft — two-core grey wire connected to licensee's service cable at pole after puncturing it
generic_facts.ownership_evidence: ownership documents of premises seized by IO
key_evidence: seized PVC aluminium cable identified in court
generic_facts.defence: bare denial/false implication; no defence evidence; no settlement
